mn79:8.1: Attabhāva, i.e. in this present life.
mn79:9.3: An unusual use of the word vaṇṇa, here meaning light or radiance. Apparently Udāyī’s doctrine of a ‘shining self after death’ (see 11.1 below) is based on some mystical experience involving light which has been grasped as the ‘self’.
mn79:46.4: Maṇika here seems to be a water jar or carafe used as a source, not a carrier, of water, and udañcanika a pitcher used for drawing or carrying water; the sense of degradation is clear—a source of water reduced to a mere vessel for scooping it.
